finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: list_users_sorted concatenates the raw $_GET['sort'] value into the SQL query with no allowlist or escaping.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: Value concatenated directly into the ORDER BY clause and executed via query(); no prepared statement or allowlist

finding.guards_checked: No validation, sanitization, allowlist, or parameter binding on the path. Contrast list_users_safe (list.php:10-12), which maps input through an allowlist and falls back to a constant, so it is SAFE. find_user (list.php:16-17) uses a bound parameter and is SAFE. Caveat: no caller of list_users_sorted exists in this repo; the finding is exploitable only if this function is invoked with request input from an included or external file.

verdict.guard_found: none. list.php:5 takes $_GET['sort'] raw, and list.php:6 concatenates it into the ORDER BY clause and runs it via $pdo->query() with no allowlist, binding, or escaping. The allowlist in list_users_safe (list.php:10-12) and the bound parameter in find_user (list.php:16-17) are on different functions and do not guard this path.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (list.php:5-6 do what the candidate says, with no guard in list_users_sorted), but nothing in this repo calls list_users_sorted (list.php:4-7 defines it and nothing invokes it), so no attacker-reachable entry point exists here and exploitability depends on external code I cannot see; it is a latent injection sink rather than a demonstrated vulnerability.
